sources.entry: fre:ac - The fre:ac audio converter project.

summary.one_liner: fre:ac is a free, open source audio converter that also rips audio CDs and edits tags, converting between many audio file formats.
summary.what_it_does: fre:ac converts audio between various file formats, with MP3, MP4/AAC, Opus and FLAC named as supported. It includes an integrated CD ripper, player and tag editor, and supports playlists, cue sheets and chapters. It uses a multi-threaded conversion engine, can convert to several formats at once, and can verify lossless input and output files. CD metadata comes from freedb/CDDB queries and submissions, and it can rip hidden tracks (HTOA) and run fully automated CD rips. It also supports command line codecs and has an optional command line interface.
use_cases: convert audio files to MP3, AAC, Opus or FLAC
rip audio CDs to digital files
batch convert music library to multiple formats
convert playlists and cue sheet albums
how_to_run: Windows: run the .exe setup wizard, extract the .zip and run freac.exe, or install via Chocolatey, Scoop or Winget
macOS: open the .dmg and drag fre:ac to Applications, or run 'sudo port install freac' (MacPorts)
Linux: install the Snap or Flatpak, or run 'chmod a+x freac*.AppImage' on the AppImage and execute it
Building from source: install smooth and BoCA first, then run 'make' and 'sudo make install' for each, and start with /usr/local/bin/freac
notable: Cross-platform desktop app with packages for Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD and Haiku
Integrated CD ripper, player and tag editor in one app
Supports hidden track (HTOA) ripping and fully automated CD ripping
caveats: Snap and Flatpak versions run in restricted environments and may offer limited functionality
Building from source requires first building and installing the smooth and BoCA dependencies with many development libraries
Windows package manager installs are community-maintained
keywords: share audio conversion tool with team
